reason: Section 189 is an oversized utility-finance provision with distinct learning topics for user-charge services, commissions and budgets, user-charge forms and collection, liens and debts, and connection or cost-allocation powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Water, sewerage, and electric services on a user-charge basis
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require or permit water, sewerage, local-improvement cost recovery and continued electric power services to operate on a user-charge basis, including classes, frontage calculations and cost-of-work content.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when municipal water, sewerage and electric services must or may be financed through user charges and how cost classes and frontage-based charges fit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Utility commissions, budgets, reserves, deficits, and surpluses
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address establishing commissions, balanced budget requirements, budget submission, deficit and surplus treatment, reserve funds, and the meaning or deemed status of commissions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how municipal utilities or commissions handle budgets, reserve funds, deficits, surpluses and commission status.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: User-charge types and by-law payment terms
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 189(8) and 189(9) define what user-charge includes and excludes, and authorize by-laws prescribing payment, collection, discounts, penalties and default proceedings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the permitted user-charge methods and the payment or enforcement terms council may prescribe by by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Water and sewer user-charge liens, debts, owner notice, and temporary borrowing
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections create a special lien for taxable land, a debt for non-taxable land, an owner-notice rule when another person owes the charges, and temporary borrowing authority for current utility expenditures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how water and sewer charges become liens or debts, when owners must be notified, and how temporary borrowing for utilities is limited.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mandatory service connections, fire-protection water costs, gas pricing, and rural-community application
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover by-laws compelling connection or charging non-connecting owners, assessment of that charge, fire-protection allocation of water costs, gas-price limits, and application to rural communities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the connection, non-connection charge, fire-protection water cost, gas-price, and rural-community application rules for section 189 services.

reason: Section 190 is a gateway authority allowing a municipality to specify by by-law the areas where sections 190.001 to 190.07 apply.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: By-law application of dangerous or unsightly premises provisions

evidenceText: may by by-law provide that sections 190.001 to 190.07 apply

proposedGroups.reason: Section 190 is a gateway authority allowing a municipality to specify by by-law the areas where sections 190.001 to 190.07 apply.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a municipal by-law may make the dangerous or unsightly premises provisions apply to prescribed areas.

reason: Section 190.001 defines dwelling and dwelling unit for sections 190.01 to 190.07 and expands owner for specified notice, appeal, work and enforcement provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Dangerous or unsightly premises definitions for dwellings and owners
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.001 defines dwelling and dwelling unit for sections 190.01 to 190.07 and expands owner for specified notice, appeal, work and enforcement provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of dwelling, dwelling unit, and owner used in the dangerous or unsightly premises provisions.

reason: Section 190.01 has distinct topics for prohibited conditions and offence penalties, and for the content of the municipal officer notice used to correct those conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unsightly premises and hazardous building prohibitions with penalties
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections prohibit unsightly premises and vacant, dilapidated or structurally unsound hazardous buildings, then set category F offence and continuing-offence fine rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prohibited dangerous or unsightly conditions and the offence and fine rules for hazardous buildings or structures.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Officer notice contents for dangerous or unsightly conditions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 190.01(3) specifies when an officer may notify an owner or occupier and what the written notice must state.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the required contents of an officer notice to correct a dangerous or unsightly premises condition.

reason: Section 190.011 sets the methods for giving a notice to an individual or corporation, including personal delivery and posting on the premises, building or structure.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service of dangerous or unsightly premises notices
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.011 sets the methods for giving a notice to an individual or corporation, including personal delivery and posting on the premises, building or structure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a section 190.01 notice must be given to individuals and corporations.

reason: Section 190.02 deals with certificates, affidavits, admissibility, conclusive proof, burden of proof, and evidentiary effect of a signed notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Proof and evidentiary effect of dangerous premises notices
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.02 deals with certificates, affidavits, admissibility, conclusive proof, burden of proof, and evidentiary effect of a signed notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how notice-giving and notice contents are proved in dangerous or unsightly premises prosecutions.

reason: Section 190.021 sets two levels of challenge to a notice and the finality and further-notice consequences, which should be studied in separate procedural groups.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appeal from officer notice to committee of council
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover the registered-mail appeal to the committee, deemed confirmation if no appeal is brought, hearing rights, municipal burden for vacant hazards, committee powers, and delivery of the decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the committee appeal steps, hearing rights, burden rule, decision powers, and deemed confirmation rule for a dangerous premises notice.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court appeal, final notice effect, and changed-condition notices
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections provide for appeal to a judge, available grounds, judge powers, final and binding effect, and the ability to issue a further notice after a changed condition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the court appeal grounds and effects, and when a further notice may still be given after an appeal.

reason: Section 190.022 defines land registration office, permits registration of a notice, deems subsequent owners to have notice, excludes Registry Act and Land Titles Act requirements, and provides certificate discharge and cancellation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration and discharge of dangerous premises notices
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.022 defines land registration office, permits registration of a notice, deems subsequent owners to have notice, excludes Registry Act and Land Titles Act requirements, and provides certificate discharge and cancellation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a dangerous premises notice may be registered, bind later owners, and be discharged or cancelled.

reason: Section 190.03 makes failure to comply with a notice an offence, sets special minimum and continuing-offence fine rules for leased dwellings or dwelling units, and preserves further prosecution for continued neglect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Offence for failing to comply with dangerous premises notice
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.03 makes failure to comply with a notice an offence, sets special minimum and continuing-offence fine rules for leased dwellings or dwelling units, and preserves further prosecution for continued neglect.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the offence, fine, continuing-offence and further-prosecution rules for failing to comply with a dangerous premises notice.
